questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Iceland offered a course on Arctic politics, which I found really interesting. At the same, I wanted to explore the culture of another nordic country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience. Iceland is a beautiful country and the icelanders are friendly. It was also very enlightening to experience a culture that is so closely connected to danish culture, and yet somewhat in opposition to Denmark/danish culture. The fact that Iceland used to be subject to Denmark is still very present in the Icelandic consciousness. University of Iceland is small university with a generally high academic level and an impressively high level of service. The only reason why I haven't rated my experience 10 is that I had one course where the academic level was just really low.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. The webpage for University of Iceland is in english.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had three introductory days where you are assigned at tutor. Furthermore, there is a help desk.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There is student housing on campus, which is not too hard to get. However, I stayed with some family friends. In generel housing in Iceland is expensive though.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to live as close to campus and/or the city center as possible. You can take the bus, but they don't come that often and they stop at every 200 meters, so it is a slow way to get around. Biking is an option, but conditions are rough.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register via the University of Iceland website for internal communication (called UGLA). Afterwards, contact the help desk. They will give you a student card. It was not difficult, but mine was a little late.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help desk.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful. I got all the classes I asked for. Even changed my schedule without problems as I found a course that sounded more interesting upon arrival.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If in doubt ask the help desk. It is the first thing you see when you enter the main building.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally very good. However, I had one course (out of 5) where the academic level was very low.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Focus on critical text analysis and class discussions. Group work and project based. Less lecture based than UCPH. In general fewer people per classroom.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Arctic Studies, Arctic Politics in International Context, Arctic Circle Assembly, Cooperation Development: Approaches and institutions and Crisis Management.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Arctic Studies, Arctic Politics in International Context, Arctic Circle Assembly and Cooperation Development: Approaches and institutions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was a gym at the university. For students it was 250 DKK for a semester. The gym itself was good - Plenty of space, new equipment. Kettlebell, running and yoga classes are also offered.

They also had different student clubs. I did not attend any of them though - It seemed they were running a bit low due to COVID-19.

On top of the they have the so-called studenterkælder, which is a pretty good restaurant/bar. Prices are fair and it is a good place to get a burger, play a board game and/or start a night out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go nuts. Everywhere you go Iceland is beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
The icelanders are easy to socialize with. Friendly. Like introducing you to their country. Maybe a bit reserved. A lot like Danes. 

Do you know anything about soccer? If so that is a good place to start :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They knew a lot more about Denmark, than I did about Iceland. Danish is their third language (Icelandic, english, danish. In that order). Their attitudes towards Denmark vary a great deal. They will not hold it against you though. Maybe you can say that some of them do not like Denmark (the state), but that most of them like the danes (the people).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are friendly and super easy-going.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring outdoor clothes (Against wind, rain, cold temperatures. In that order. Beautiful country, rough conditions), make an effort to interact with the icelanders themselves (not just other exchange students), focus on the courses you find interesting.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go explore :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a better understanding of a different culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not enough time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
